title: Yankee Swap
logline: Corporate's headcount audit sends Michael into a gift-giving panic, while Jim and Pam's fake David Wallace email sends Dwight into a 3 p.m. frenzy and the office quietly writes Michael a letter of support.
outline: A: Michael hears Corporate (Gerald Boyd) is auditing headcount; he writes kind-but-awful recommendation letters for everyone, then brings a Yankee Swap gift box of personal cards that nobody takes until the office rallies. B: Jim and Pam fake a David Wallace invite for Dwight's 3 p.m. call; Dwight takes it seriously; they confess and Dwight frames it. C: Angela and Kelly split the Party Planning Committee; Oscar figures out Angela and Dwight and says nothing. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, B, C, A, B, A, C, tag.
theme: Being seen: people show their love in clumsy, backwards ways, and the only real gift is attention.
storySoFar: Stanley's countdown is at 200. Michael is nervous that Corporate's audit (Gerald Boyd) will cut Scranton headcount, and he is trying to win everyone's love before the review. The Christmas party is December 21 with a Yankee Swap; Angela runs the Party Planning Committee, and Kelly has split off to start a rival subcommittee with Phyllis. Jim and Pam keep pranking Dwight, who is Acting RM by memo and in an armed truce with Andy; Dwight and Andy won Lenny Zorn's account together. Jim brought Shannon to the Office Outing and Pam is unsettled; Jim still has not said what he wants to say. Roy cancelled again. Kevin and Oscar know about Angela and Dwight and say nothing. Michael's Things I Love board holds Dwight's 61%, Kevin's M&Ms note, Dale's card, and Pam's drawing of Michael running.

stateChanges.progress: Corporate headcount audit threatens Scranton. Michael's kind-but-awful recommendation letters and his Yankee Swap box of cards fail, then the office rallies by giving him their gifts. Secret letters to Gerald Boyd are being written behind his back. Gerald says headcount is unchanged for now and to bring receipts.
Dwight is pranked into a fake 3 p.m. David Wallace call; Andy is quietly dismissive. Armed truce holds.
Oscar has figured it out from the beets and is keeping it to himself, annoyed. Kevin knows too. Nobody says anything.

stateChanges.arc: Will They, Won't They: Jim and Pam
stateChanges.progress: Pam and Jim prank Dwight together; the prank is their first real collaboration since Shannon. Jim has not yet said what he means; Pam saw the framed prank as a sign of trust.

stateChanges.text: Stanley's countdown: 200 in the cold open, 199 in the tag; Michael's 'That's what she said' lands on silence; Kevin: 'Nobody say nothing.'
Dwight frames the prank next to the Post-it in his desk drawer; it counts as evidence.
Michael's Things I Love board: the office's secret letters to Gerald Boyd praise Michael; pay off in the finale when Corporate's review ends in his favor.
Gerald Boyd has a stack of 'letters' with no receipts. Tag sets the finale.
Michael's Yankee Swap box holds personal index cards for everyone; Kelly, Dwight and Stanley read theirs. Michael's card for Toby called him 'present'.

scenes.recap: Stanley hits 200 days and Michael's joke lands on silence, and Kevin gets the last word.

beats.text: Two hundred days.
Two hundred? Stanley, that's what she said.

beats.caption: Stanley does not look up from his crossword.

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.

scenes.recap: Michael announces the Yankee Swap and tells the office Corporate's auditor is coming to count heads.

beats.text: Christmas party, December twenty-first. Yankee Swap, twenty dollars, and I want warm bodies. Corporate loves warm bodies.
The Party Planning Committee has approved a Holiday Gala theme. Black tie optional.
Optional for who? Ugly sweaters are iconic now, Angela.
Okay, let's not fight about the sweaters. Gerald Boyd from corporate auditing is coming to review us. Headcount.
Michael, I'm not allowed to discuss personnel matters in a—
You're not allowed to talk, Toby. I'm talking.
Question: are we the two positions? False. Scranton has no positions. It has an Acting Regional Manager.
Thank you, Dwight. Nobody is getting cut. We are going to make everyone feel loved, so when Corporate looks at a spreadsheet, they see faces.

lines: I'm not scared. I'm reorganizing my fear into a party.
Two positions. I could be one of them. I'm also the other one, I think.

scenes.recap: Jim and Pam plan a fake David Wallace invite for Dwight's 3 p.m. call.

beats.text: Dwight is going to think Corporate called him.
Dwight is going to think Corporate called him. That's the whole prank.
You can't fake David Wallace. He'll know it's fake.
Not David. His assistant. Nobody has ever met his assistant.

beats.caption: sets a Dunder letterhead on the table and aligns the logo by eye

beats.text: It's on letterhead. Dwight will want to frame it before he reads it.
Three p.m. He has to prepare. He'll be insufferable for two hours.
Is this too far?
Only if he finds the Jell-O.

lines: Jim makes elaborate fake emails. I make them look real. That's our whole relationship, honestly.
I'm not saying it's a love language. I'm saying it's a font.

scenes.recap: Kelly quits Angela's committee and starts a subcommittee with Phyllis, while Angela leans on Dwight and Oscar notices.

beats.text: Kelly. The committee rejected Ugly Sweater Pop.
It wasn't rejected, it was not reviewed. There's a difference, Angela.
Ryan is DJing. He already picked the playlist.
Ryan is not on the committee.
Ryan is on everything! Then I quit the committee. I'm starting the Kelly Kapoor Holiday Subcommittee.
I'm in. I'll bring Bob's fondue.
You can't start a subcommittee of two.
It's three if Ryan counts. Phyllis, get the cheese.
Dwight, thank you for verifying the cups. You're very helpful.
Acting approval. Helpfulness is a Schrute trait.

scenes.recap: Michael writes kind but terrible recommendation letters for everyone, starting with Toby.

beats.text: Toby, sit. I'm writing letters for Corporate. For everybody. So they can't cut us.

beats.caption: scribbles on Dunder letterhead and misspells 'receipt'

beats.text: You can't write letters on company letterhead. It's a—
Yes you can. Sit. Yours is first.
'Toby Flenderson is present.' That's the whole first line.
Present?
Present is good! Corporate loves present. Then: 'We would miss his sad sighs.'
That's... actually that's a compliment?

beats.caption: Michael looks at what he wrote and softens.

beats.text: He's also the only one who asks me if I'm okay. Don't tell anybody.

lines: He wrote me a recommendation. It says I'm present.
I've been here six years. I'm going to frame it next to the fire code.

beats.text: Thank you, Michael.
Don't make it weird. Go get Pam her letter.

scenes.recap: Dwight receives a letter about a 3 p.m. call with David Wallace and decides to prepare, with Jim as his witness.

beats.caption: holds the printed letter up to the window to check the watermark

beats.text: Question: why is David Wallace's office inviting me to a 3 p.m. call re: Christmas bonus pipeline?
Dwight, that sounds like a scam. Also 'pipeline' is a word I used once.
False. Corporate does not scam. Corporate sends letters.
Jim, you are my witness.
Sure. Witness.

beats.caption: dials Corporate's main number from memory and asks for a Jan

beats.text: Oh no.
It's fine. He's dialing Stamford.
Did I stutter? Dwight, do it quietly.
I need a suit, Jim. Corporate has noticed me.

lines: Corporate has been noticing me for six years. Jim is my witness, which means he is jealous.
I will be on that call for ninety minutes, and no one in this building will have a thing to say about it.

scenes.recap: Angela drops by accounting and Kevin almost says it; Oscar shuts him down and admits he knows.

beats.text: Oscar, Dwight is handling the Yankee Swap rules. He's Acting.
Of course he is.
Angela like Dwight. Dwight like Angela. Beets.
Kevin. Not here.
Excuse me?
Nothing. Kevin has a chili concern.
Chili is concern.
Nobody says anything.
Nobody say nothing.

lines: I figured it out on a Tuesday, from the beets. I'm the only adult in this building who isn't saying anything.
It is exhausting. I am telling you, the camera, which does not count.

scenes.recap: The Yankee Swap: Michael's box of personal cards goes untouched, and the office gives him their gifts instead.

beats.text: Rules: you pick a gift, you can be stolen from three times. Dwight is in charge of the bell.
Acting. I am in charge of the bell.

beats.caption: steals a gift from Ryan and waves it over her head

beats.text: Dwight, Yankee means steal. I'm stealing your candle.
Theft. That was a Schrute family candle.
My gift is this one. It's for whoever ends up with it.

beats.caption: Nobody takes the box. It's labeled FOR WHOEVER.

beats.text: Is it homework?
It's not homework. It's cards. Just cards. About each of you.
Can we go now?
That's fine. It's a Christmas tradition to be ignored. I'll open it later. Alone. Like a grown man.

beats.caption: Michael picks up the box and puts it down again.

beats.text: Okay. I'll take it. Ryan, you're going to pay for this.

beats.caption: pulls out a card and reads it silently, then looks away

beats.text: 'Kelly, you're the loudest person I love.' Okay. That's so weird.
Question: is there a card for me?
It says you're the most loyal person I have ever met.
False. It says I am inaccurate. Oh. It's a good inaccuracy.

beats.caption: slides his pretzel tin across the table to Michael

beats.text: Take the pretzels. Do not say a word.
Michael, take the candle. It's Jan's. Don't tell Jan.
Actually, the candle is a Serenity by Jan. You should keep it.
Michael, we'll do a song. Dwight, it's Christmas.
Banned.
Thank you, guys. This is a meeting now. I'm not crying. Dunder Mifflin doesn't allow tears in meetings.
That's not a rule.
Michael. M&Ms.

scenes.recap: Dwight finds the printer log, frames the fake letter, and tells Jim and Pam they went too far.

beats.text: Question: who printed a letter on Dunder letterhead with a fake David Wallace signature?
Pam printed it.
Jim, I did the font.
The font is correct. That is what makes it dangerous.
I called Corporate. Jan's assistant said 'Who?' False. There was no 3 p.m.
We're sorry, Dwight.
Don't be sorry. Be a witness.
I'm framing it. It goes next to the Post-it in my drawer. It's evidence now.
You're framing it?
It is the best prank ever played on me. I was almost selected.
I'll be watching you. Like a sheriff.
We went too far.
Yeah. But he's keeping it. That's a compliment.

lines: Dwight called Corporate, which was a mistake. Now Jan's assistant has his fax number.
Pam says we went too far. I'd say we went exactly far enough to be in the same room for an hour.

scenes.recap: The office is secretly writing letters to Gerald Boyd praising Michael, and Michael walks in on them.

beats.text: Dear Gerald. Michael Scott is the reason I stayed.
Keep it factual. Michael is organized in his own way.
Actually, 'organized in his own way' is a threat to Corporate.
Kevin write Michael is good boss. Kevin write Michael has candy.

beats.caption: slides the letters under a sticky-note drawing as the door opens

beats.text: What are you guys doing?
Party menu.
Why is it in Gerald font?
Actually, it's a seating chart. We're seating you by the door.
Did I stutter? Go away, Michael.
Okay. Okay. I'm going to my office where I can write my own letters.
Did we just lie to him?
Nobody say nothing.

lines: Everyone's acting weird. Either it's a surprise party or I'm getting fired.
Okay, I'd prefer a surprise party. I've had a lot of firings. I've never had a seating chart.

scenes.recap: Angela calls a truce with Kelly over the sweaters and gives her the clipboard.

beats.text: I'm sorry about the sweater thing, Kelly.
Thank you, Angela. That's the nicest thing you've ever said to me.

beats.caption: hands Kelly a clipboard with a pink pen clipped to it

beats.text: Ryan can DJ. Phyllis, the fondue stays in the kitchen.
Bob's bringing the cheese. He insists. It's his cheese.
Don't tell Dwight about the cups.
Why would I tell Dwight anything?
Forget I said it.

lines: I am not in love with anyone. I am the only organized person in a building full of people who can't count to twenty.
Dwight counts to twenty without a calculator. I didn't say that.

scenes.recap: Gerald Boyd receives a stack of letters about Michael, asks for receipts, and Stanley's countdown hits 199.

beats.text: I'm here for the Scranton branch review.
Gerald! Welcome. I have some letters.
Is there a receipt for the letters?
They're letters. They don't come with receipts.
Eleven say 'Michael is the reason I stayed.' Two say 'Michael is a boss.' One says 'Kevin.'
Do not be happy. Headcount is unchanged. For now. Bring me receipts.
One hundred ninety-nine.
Stanley, that's what she said.

beats.caption: Stanley looks straight into the camera.

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.
